text:
alexc: Quick question — I'm about to land a small terraform change that flips some subnets to route 0.0.0.0/0 -> new egress-proxy NLB instead of AZ NAT GW. PR here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/489. Can someone sanity-check routing precedence with PrivateLink endpoints?

tessm: @alexc are these interface endpoints or gateway endpoints? that matters for route table behavior.

alexc: interface endpoints (com.amazonaws.*) — no gateway endpoint changes. My concern is we have explicit 0.0.0.0/0 to NLB in the private subnet route table; if a consumer tries to reach a PrivateLink service (to partner), traffic should hit the ENI for the endpoint IPs — but want to make sure there's no accidental catch-all.

jordanp: In practice interface endpoints allocate ENIs in the subnet and use the local routing table; explicit 0.0.0.0/0 shouldn't override an IP-specific route. But double-check the terraform code — if you add a 0.0.0.0/0 that points to the NLB via an attachment, make sure we don't also create a broad security group that blocks the ENI. :thinking:

alexc: pasted the key snippet from the PR plan:```hcl
resource "aws_route" "egress_to_nlb" {
  for_each = var.egress_nlb_enabled ? toset(var.private_subnet_ids) : {}
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.private[each.value].id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  network_interface_id   = aws_network_interface.egress_nlb_enis[each.value].id
}
```

tessm: hmm `network_interface_id` on a route is valid for some setups but are you sure the NLB will present an eni for each subnet? usually NLB targets are ip/eni targets but routing to an eni is fragile. we usually point to a natgateway id or transit gateway attachment. Why NLB route vs nat gateway?

alexc: we want to funnel outbound to an egress proxy service that inspects+logs traffic. NLB -> proxy pods (host network) is how we did it in a prototype. This avoids per-AZ nat cost. The proxy team confirmed sticky per-AZ ENIs will exist.

priya: if we do this, can we add a canary var so only a subset of subnets use the new route? we should also add healthcheck fallback so if proxy unhealthy we fall back to AZ NAT.

jordanp: agree. Add `egress_nlb_canary_subnet_ids` var and a `count`/`for_each` to limit. Also add a `local` that assembles fallback routes: if NLB target_health != healthy then route -> natgw. Might be a bit of a manual check since terraform doesn't query target group health at plan time.

alexc: yep plan currently adds routes for two subnets (canary). CI plan output: `Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.` I'm going to add documentation to the subnet module explaining the precedence and failure modes.

tf-plan-bot: terraform plan for infra/egress in PR #489 — success — no apply yet.

tessm: small nit — call out that interface endpoint ENIs have IPs in the subnet CIDR. If any ip route overlaps (e.g., you added a host route for a /24), traffic to endpoint IPs could be affected. Also double-check the security group on the ENI for the proxy; it needs to allow inbound from the subnet CIDR or service network.

alexc: good catch. I'll add a check to ensure no host routes that overlap endpoint IPs and add the canary var + fallback plan. Will also ping the proxy owners for SG review. Thanks all.

priya: lgtm — please add a short rollback playbook in the PR body (how to revert routes quickly).

alexc: will do, pushing an update now. thanks! :thumbsup:
